chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:

He heard him saying: 'Verily, the Prophet Dāwūd (peace be upon him) was once in his prayer niche when a small red worm crept by until it came to the place of his prostration. Dāwūd looked at it and said to himself, “Why was this worm created?” So Allah inspired it, “Speak!” So it said to him, “O Dāwūd, have you heard my sound as I move, or have you noticed my tracks on the smooth earth?” Dāwūd replied, “No.” So it said, “Verily Allah hears my crawl, my breathing, and my sound, and He sees the tracks of my movement, so lower your voice.”'

key_terms.مِحْرَاب: prayer niche or place of worship

ai.seo_question: What lesson did Prophet Dāwūd learn from the red worm regarding humility and divine observation?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the concept of *khushu'* (humility) by illustrating that divine awareness extends even to the minute movements of a small worm, thereby challenging the Prophet Dāwūd’s self-perception. It serves as a profound reminder for believers that true piety involves maintaining God-consciousness (*taqwa*) in private acts of worship, not just in public display. The story underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on purifying the heart from subtle forms of self-admiration (*riya'* al-khafiyya).
